full_judgment:
2. Respondent No.1 was the Manager of the Rupali Bank, Branch at Fakirapool while the said Bank was a nationalised Bank. Respondent Nos.2 and 3 are the wives of the respondent No.1. Respondent No.1 was dismissed from service for resorting to corruption. He filed Title Suit No.2 of 1989 and the same was decreed on July 12, 1990. He submitted joining report on July 17, 1990 but the same was not accepted. The Bank filed appeal being Title Appeal No.239 of 1990 and the same was dismissed on August 11, 1993. Thereupon the Bank moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction, Civil Revision No. 3277 of 1993 and the Rule was discharged on March 8, 1999. The Bank filed appeal, Civil Appeal No.69 of 1999, and this Division allowed the appeal by the judgment dated October 31, 2001. The ordering portion of the judgment of this Division runs as: 

 "In the result, the appeal is allowed without cost. The judgment dated 8-3-1999 passed by High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3277 of 1993 are set aside and consequently both the judgments and decrees of the courts below are set aside. Title Suit No.2 of 1989 of the Court of Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No.2, Dhaka; is dismissed without cost". 

 10. The learned Counsel for the appellant submits that although the respondent No.1 was an employee of the nationalished Bank and, as such, was a public servant but with the denationalisation of the Bank by the Gazette Notification dated April 6, 1987 in spite of the decree in the Title Suit No.2 of 1989 declaring the dismissal order of the respondent No.1 not legal, the respondent No.1 having had ceased to be a public servant upon nationalisation the High Court Division was in error in quashing the proceedings of the Special Case No. 12 of 1985 on the view that because of the judgment in the Title Suit No. 2 of 1989 and maintaining thereof up to the High Court Division level the respondent No.1 was continuing in the service of the Bank and, as such, for prosecution of the said respondent sanction of the Government was very much necessary. 

 11. The learned Additional Attorney-General submitted that as against the judgment of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3277 of 1993 filed against the judgment and decree passed in Title Appeal No. 239 of 1990 affirming the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.2 of 1989 the Bank filed Civil Appeal No. 69 of 1999 and this Division by the judgment dated October 31, 2001 allowed the appeal upon setting aside the judgment passed in the civil revision and thereupon dismissed the Title Suit No.2 of 1989 and in the aforesaid state of the matter no sanction is necessary for the prosecution of the respondent No.1 since order of dismissal passed in respect of the respondent No.1 has been found valid and, as such, respondent No.1 ceased to be an employee of the Bank on and from the date of dismissal i.e. on 25-5-1987.
